description:
deviation.rs DeviationStore::find_deviation and find_deviation_for_chain iterate self.deviations linearly on every call. The runner calls find_deviation per Finding, so a chain with N findings against a store of M deviations is O(N*M) per chain.

In the typical operator setup (M < 50 deviations, N < 100 findings per chain), this is fine. At the workspace-batch shape (replaying many chains against the same store), the cost is M * total_findings.

Cheap optimization: build a HashMap<target_lint, Vec<&Deviation>> at first lookup (lazy_init) so find_deviation does O(1) lint-id lookup plus O(matching_deviations) scope-match. Most lint ids have zero or one matching deviation in the store; the speedup is roughly M-fold for the common case.

Not P0 — workspace tests stay under threshold. Worth filing so future batch-mode work has a starting point. Also see AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 'callbacks not closed structs' — DeviationStore is the closed struct, but its lookup shape is the bottleneck if it ever becomes one.
title: DeviationStore lookups are linear; cache-friendly index recommended at scale
